Text_Content: Driven by the rapid development of the low-altitude economy, Uncrewed Aerial Vehicle (UAV) networks have become increasingly important for executing tasks such as search, rescue, and monitoring. However, under bandwidth-constrained scenarios, UAV networks still face significant challenges in task execution efficiency and intelligent processing capabilities. To address these issues, we propose Multi-UAV Cooperative Deep Semantic Autoencoders (MC-DSA) for communication networks. The architecture comprises one Task UAV (T-UAV) and multiple Support UAVs (S-UAVs), which jointly enhance communication efficiency and data-processing capability via semantic communication and cooperation. Specifically, we introduce a semantic matching and source selection mechanism, enabling the proposed MC-DSA to handle low-quality images while ensuring effective utilization of high-quality images. The T-UAV broadcasts a task query, and each S-UAV computes the semantic similarity between its local image and the query. Communication links are established only when the similarity exceeds a predefined threshold. The training algorithm optimizes network parameters through gradient descent, improving semantic feature extraction accuracy. The testing algorithm evaluates UAV collaboration efficiency and communication quality. Experimental results demonstrate that, compared with benchmarks, the proposed MC-DSA improves image semantic segmentation accuracy while maintaining task execution efficiency. As a result, it reduces redundant transmissions and offers an effective solution for multi-UAV communication networks.

Title: EnvOpt: Automated Optimization for Agent Environments
Author: Mingxuan Li, Huanzhi Mao, Qiuyang Mang, Hanchen Li, Joseph E. Gonzalez, Alex Dimakis
Text_Content: An LLM agent's cost and success depend on its model, its harness, and its environment. In addition to the widely studied directions of parameter tuning and harness optimization, we propose the third direction: optimization over stationary environments. Agents are often deployed in rich environments shared by many tasks, such as a company's Slack workspace or a complex collection of data sources, documents or tickets. We call these environments stationary environments. We introduce EnvOpt, a method for automated end-to-end optimization of stationary environments for any given model and harness, using real or synthetic tasks without needing any graders or reference answers. On AutomationBench, EnvOpt reduces the cost of Claude Haiku 4.5 by 72.7% and raises its pass rate by 14.34%. The same environment transfers to Opus 5, cutting its cost by 68.1% with a 1.34% gain. Added on top of Meta-Harness's optimized harness for Haiku 4.5, it lowers cost by a further 83.4% and adds 11.17% accuracy over Meta-Harness alone. Across 5 benchmarks, EnvOpt significantly reduces the cost of agents while improving or maintaining pass rate, and is transferable to different models and different harnesses. We also discuss common successful and rejected environment optimization strategies during automated optimization. More broadly, our results show that how information is represented to an agent shapes both its cost and its success, making the environment worth optimizing in addition to the parameters and the harness.

Title: Breaking $\mathsf{TraintoDefend}$ via Adaptive Neuron Clustering in Cryptanalytic Model Extraction
Author: Haojie Wu, Haolin Liu, Tianshuo Cong, Guoyan Zhang
Text_Content: Cryptanalytic model extraction poses a fundamental threat to deep learning model confidentiality by enabling precise parameter recovery with theoretical guarantees of functional equivalence. To counter this growing threat, $\mathsf{TraintoDefend}$ (NeurIPS 2025) was proposed as the first dedicated defense against cryptanalytic extraction and remains the only defense believed to be effective to date. It encourages neurons to learn similar weights so that they switch activation states together, making their individual contributions harder to distinguish. However, we notice that neurons with similar weights need not switch activation states together under small perturbations. Instead, weight similarity can cause the original clustering rule to merge signatures from distinct neurons when only a subset of their normalized weight coordinates agree. Motivated by this observation, we introduce $\mathsf{SimBreak}$, an adaptive clustering rule that breaks the weight-similarity defense of $\mathsf{TraintoDefend}$. $\mathsf{SimBreak}$ estimates a relative scale from all jointly observed weight coordinates and uses the same scale to test both weight direction and bias consistency. Across six protected fully connected networks trained on MNIST, $\mathsf{SimBreak}$ raises target layer signature recovery from $0\%$ to $100\%$, with a maximum relative recovery error of $2^{-22.27}$. Our work challenges the use of neuron weight similarity as a sufficient basis for protection and establishes adaptive evaluation as essential to assessing cryptanalytic extraction defenses.

Title: A Simple Discrete Newton Method for the Quickest Transshipment Problem
Author: Naoyuki Kamiyama
Text_Content: The quickest transshipment problem is a problem defined in a dynamic network with multiple sources and multiple sinks. The goal of this problem is to send all the supplies from sources to sinks as quickly as possible. It is known that this problem can be solved in polynomial time. In particular, Schlöter, Skutella, and Tran proposed a strongly polynomial-time discrete Newton method for this problem. In this paper, we propose a simple polynomial-time discrete Newton method for the quickest transshipment problem.

Title: Test-Time Self-Play: Scaling without a Verifier
Author: Akira Yoshiyama, Akmal Ashirmatov, Jonas Hübotter, Ido Hakimi, Andreas Krause
Text_Content: Test-time scaling methods spend additional compute at deployment to improve a large language model's performance on a hard target problem. Most methods rely on a verifier that scores candidate solutions for correctness, using it to select among or refine the model's outputs. In many deployment regimes, however, a strong verifier on the target problem is unavailable. We introduce Test-Time Self-Play (TTSP), an approach to test-time scaling using asymmetric self-play without reliance on a verifier. On a difficulty-calibrated subset of LiveCodeBench v6, TTSP is the best-performing method at every verifier strength we evaluate, and the gap to the strongest baseline widens as the verifier weakens; in the no-verifier limit, TTSP yields a 35\% absolute improvement in mean@8. The gains hold across a range of verifier strengths, except when the base policy has near-zero coverage of the correct answer.

Title: Asymptotic-Preserving Tensor Neural Networks for 3D High-Field Kinetic Equations with Applications to Uncertainty Quantification
Author: Shi Jin, Tian-ai Zhang
Text_Content: Kinetic equations in the high-field regime describe particle transport dominated by electric-field acceleration and collisional relaxation. These equations are widely used in simulations of plasmas and semiconductor devices. Typical models include the Vlasov--Poisson--Fokker--Planck (VPFP) and Boltzmann--Poisson systems. Their high dimensionality and multiscale nature pose two of the major challenges to accurate and efficient numerical solution. To address these challenges, we propose an asymptotic-preserving tensor neural network (APTNN) method. Specifically, to reduce high-dimensional computational costs and memory requirements, we adopt the canonical polyadic (CP) decomposition structure of TNNs to approximate their solutions. We show that the equation residuals retain this decomposition form, allowing high-dimensional loss integrals to be evaluated through combinations of one-dimensional integrals. The resulting computational and storage costs are reduced from exponential to polynomial growth with dimension. To improve the prediction accuracy in the high-field limit, we enhance the baseline AP loss by incorporating the first moment equation. The added loss term directly constrains the limiting flux closure to reduce its approximation error in the high-field regime. The enhanced AP loss can still be evaluated dimension-wise. Numerical results show that APTNN improves prediction accuracy in the high-field regime with significantly reduced computational costs and memory usage. For a 3D3V VPFP problem with multiple random inputs, training takes less than 30 minutes on a single GPU.

Title: Design of a Speech Enhancement-Based Deep Semantic Autoencoder for Wireless Communications
Author: Xiaoling Han, Bin Lin, Nan Wu, Tony Q. S. Quek
Text_Content: Speech communication plays a crucial role in the Internet of Things and autonomous networks. However, traditional communication systems suffer from insufficient semantic extraction and limited noise suppression capability. To address these issues, we propose a Speech enhancement-based Deep Semantic Autoencoder (S-DSA) communication system for wireless communications. It consists of a dual-branch semantic encoder, a channel encoder, a channel decoder, and two semantic decoders, enabling joint source-channel coding for robust transmission. A key novelty lies in an adaptive semantic noise decoupling mechanism that disentangles target speech semantics from noise representations through an interaction module, thus maintaining semantic consistency under low SNR conditions. Furthermore, a joint training strategy optimizes speech reconstruction and noise estimation, while a lightweight testing strategy reduces complexity by disabling the noise-decoding path. The proposed S-DSA enables more effective separation between speech and noise, and yields higher robustness as well as better reconstruction quality. These findings highlight the potential of the proposed S-DSA as a practical solution for next-generation intelligent wireless communications.

Title: Energy-conserving scheme for a shallow-water model with capillary effects
Author: K. Sudarshan Kumar, Boniface Nkonga, Praveen Chandrashekar
Text_Content: We consider numerical approximations of shallow-water and thin-film flow models with capillary effects. These models lead to third-order differential equations, and we work with an augmented model with second-order derivatives. For a wide class of such models, which includes the classical shallow-water model and thin-film flow models under gravitational force, we develop a fully discrete energy-conserving scheme for both the quadratic and fully nonlinear capillary models. Numerical results show that the proposed scheme is stable and conserves total energy in the absence of dissipative effects.

Title: A Synchronized Tri-Modality Wireless System for Multi-Point Non-Contact Cardiac Monitoring
Author: Wei Ren, Kaili Zhao, Huansheng Yi, Miaoyang Hu, Jianqi Wang, Canhua Xu, Fugui Qi
Text_Content: Cardiac physiological monitoring is fundamental to evaluating cardiovascular health and diagnosing related diseases. Non-contact radar sensing can capture chest-wall vibrations with spatial specificity, enabling localized physiological monitoring and cardiac assessment. Progress, however, has been limited by the absence of a reliable, research-grade hardware platform for rigorous validation of radar-based methods. Prior systems typically pair radar, namely Doppler cardiography (DCG), with only electrocardiography (ECG) or other coarse references, providing no direct mechanical ground truth and thus constraining fine-grained evaluation of radar outputs. We present a tri-modality wireless system that integrates ECG, seismocardiography (SCG), and DCG under a unified acquisition and control framework for time-aligned recording and analysis. The tri-modality system combines miniaturized wearable ECG/SCG modules with a high-resolution mmWave radar module, supporting spatially resolved sensing and subsequent feature extraction. To our knowledge, this is the first integrated ECG--SCG--DCG hardware system for comprehensive cardiac monitoring; it enables multi-point thoracic acquisition, achieves precise cross-modal synchronization, and maintains specifications suitable for wearable operation. Experiments on a linear-motion platform show close agreement between DCG- and SCG-derived displacements, confirming accurate displacement measurement. Human-subject studies further demonstrate cross-modal consistency and robust extraction of feature points, establishing ECG as the electrical anchor and SCG as the mechanical ground truth for DCG. Overall, the system provides a rigorous, spatially resolved validation platform that advances non-contact cardiac sensing and supports next-generation radar-based monitoring.

Title: Evaluation of Image Noise from Computed Tomography in an Organ-Specific Anthropomorphic Phantom
Author: Lucas McCullum, Mojtaba Zarei, Andy Tsai, Michael J. Callahan, Peng Sun, Da Zhang
Text_Content: Computed tomography (CT) is used ubiquitously for diagnostic imaging, with novel iterative reconstructions such as hybrid iterative reconstruction with partial model-based component (ASiR-V) and deep learning image reconstruction (DLIR) increasingly utilized. In conjunction, CT vendors have developed a noise index (NI) to reduce radiation dose during protocol development. However, it is unclear how these reconstruction algorithms reduce noise as NI changes, particularly across multiple organs. The goal of this study was to utilize an anthropomorphic phantom to evaluate image noise against the prescribed NI across different organs, determine if DLIR reduces image noise compared to ASiR-V, and use this relationship to determine the maximum volume CT dose index (CTDIvol) reduction at equivalent noise levels. Repeat images were acquired on a GE HealthCare Revolution Apex CT scanner across NI values in an anthropomorphic adult-sized phantom from Kyoto Kagaku with ASiR-V and DLIR. Organs-of-interest were contoured using TotalSegmentator in 3D Slicer. The correlation between the CTDIvol and NI was determined. The standard deviation of the difference in the repeat images was used as a noise metric (NM), correlated with NI, used to determine the NI at equivalent NM between ASiR-V and DLIR, then applied to determine the dose reduction and difference in NM. The relationship between NI and the resulting CTDIvol was found to be proportional to a power law of exponent -2.23. The maximum potential absolute dose reduction from using DLIR was found in the liver at 1.3 mGy with an NI of 7.9. Across all organs, the relative dose reduction increased, the NM-to-NI ratio decreased, and the noise reduction increased across NI. The relationship between image noise and the prescribed NI differed between ASiR-V and DLIR and varied by organ, with model-based dose reductions of up to 1.3 mGy in the liver.

Title: Acoustic Anomaly Detection for Early Identification of Drill Jamming
Author: Maria Beatriz Silva, Lucas Edson Silva de Araújo, Sergio F. Chevtchenko, Ermeson Andrade, Danilo Araujo, Saeed Afshar
Text_Content: In the context of Industry 4.0, predictive maintenance is essential to minimize unplanned downtime and ensure operational safety. In machining processes, drill jamming is a critical failure that compromises both workpiece quality and tool integrity. This work proposes an acoustic anomaly detection system using ultrasonic sensors to identify pre-failure patterns in Computer Numerical Control (CNC) machining. We release a public dataset of time- and frequency-domain acoustic features from 17 drills, and benchmark semi-supervised autoencoder-based normality modelling against supervised XGBoost classification using Leave-One-Drill-Out validation. The results demonstrate that the Autoencoder is highly effective for industrial safety, achieving a Recall of 1.00 and a consolidated F1-score of 0.81. Furthermore, the threshold-independent analysis shows that the Autoencoder better separates normal and pre-failure acoustic patterns, achieving a consolidated AUC of 0.8294, compared with 0.7559 for the supervised model under inter-tool covariate shift. In contrast, the supervised XGBoost achieved an average F1-score of 0.55 and failed to detect failures in some of the evaluated drills. The findings highlight that the ultrasonic spectrum provides a reliable window for identifying incipient mechanical instabilities, and the AE model offers a robust safety envelope by anticipating all jamming events across the tested drill bits.

Title: Constant-Factor Approximation Algorithms for Weighted Budgeted Multisensor Sweep Coverage
Author: Jingyang Zhao, Jason William Setiawan, Uman Khalid, Chaoning Zhang, Een-Kee Hong, Hyundong Shin
Text_Content: Sweep coverage requires each point of interest (PoI) to be revisited by some mobile sensor at least once during every sweep period, and it underlies persistent patrolling, environmental monitoring, and infrastructure inspection. Given a set of $N$ PoIs, each associated with a nonnegative weight representing its importance, the weighted budgeted sweep coverage problem (WB-SCP) seeks routing trajectories for a budget of $M\leq N$ identical mobile sensors with a common maximum speed to maximize the total weight of the sweep-covered PoIs. For the unweighted special case in which every PoI has unit weight, the first constant-factor approximation algorithm achieves a ratio of $0.0116-O(\varepsilon)$ for any constant $\varepsilon>0$, and whether the WB-SCP itself admits such an algorithm has remained open. In this paper, we resolve this open question by proposing two constant-factor approximation algorithms for the WB-SCP. The first converts any bifactor $(α,β)$-approximation algorithm into a $β/(2α)$-approximation algorithm, yielding a ratio of $1/16=0.0625$. The second builds on a greedy maximum-coverage framework and improves the ratio to $1-e^{-1/2}-\varepsilon$ for any fixed $\varepsilon>0$. Both algorithms also improve the best-known ratio for the unweighted case, and the second extends to heterogeneous sensors with different speeds while preserving the same guarantee.

Title: MIKU: Material Invariance and Knowledge Unification for PBR Generation
Author: Yajie Bao, Jiaye Fu, Youtian Lin, Shuang Wu, Jiachen Qian, Feihu Zhang, Xun Cao, Yao Yao
Text_Content: High-quality material generation for physically based rendering (PBR) remains challenging because datasets and synthesis pipelines lack standardized representations. Differences in material definitions, rendering conventions, and parameterizations lead to unstable and physically implausible results. We propose MIKU, a unified framework for standardized PBR asset representation and physically consistent material generation across diverse 3D content domains. Its core is a unified processing pipeline that standardizes the workflow from data preprocessing to final texture synthesis, maintaining consistent geometry and texture representations. A normalization scheme harmonizes heterogeneous material parameterizations in a common representation space, enabling robust cross-dataset training and inference. Building on this formulation, we train a novel physically aware diffusion model for PBR texture generation within a two-stage multi-view synthesis framework. First, geometry-aware albedo generation synthesizes multi-view albedo maps under explicit geometric guidance to ensure cross-view appearance consistency. Second, metallic-roughness generation uses the diffusion model to predict physically plausible roughness and metallic maps conditioned on the generated albedo and unified representation. Trained end-to-end on standardized data, the model learns to generate materials that respect category-level material priors and semantic part boundaries. By decoupling representation standardization from appearance synthesis, MIKU substantially improves material generation stability and physical consistency. Extensive experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art texture quality and semantic consistency across object parts, advancing automated material generation for 3D content creation.

Title: Analysis of Xe-131 Prompt Gammas
Author: Andrew Rosen, Jacob Moldenhauer, Caterina Michelagnoli, Marek Stryjczyk, Will Flanagan
Text_Content: The prompt gammas of Xe-131 from thermal neutron capture were measured for the first time at the Fission Product Prompt gamma-ray Spectrometer by irradiation of isotopically enriched Xe-130 in a high-purity quartz ampoule. Through gamma-gamma coincidences, 42 new prompt gammas were measured and 14 new nuclear states determined.

Title: From What Is Used to What Is Missing: Rethinking Dynamic Rank in LoRA
Author: Peng Xue, Guodong Fan, Guang-Yong Chen, Xing Chen
Text_Content: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning with LoRA is governed by rank, which controls parameter budget and locally accessible task updates. Existing dynamic-rank methods mainly focus on capacity allocation, leaving unresolved whether the current adaptation space is sufficient for the task. We characterize the first-order information boundary of standard factor gradients, showing that their unobservable subspace coincides with the normal space of the low-rank manifold. Thus, factor gradients alone cannot distinguish under-optimization within the current space from task-relevant directions beyond its first-order reach. This motivates a geometric view of rank evolution, where tangent information optimizes existing degrees of freedom and the normal spectrum quantifies the value of new ones. Under a local quadratic model, we show that leading normal singular directions yield the locally optimal rank expansion, with spectral energy determining its gain. Building on this characterization, we propose GEAR, which turns the tangent--normal decomposition into rank evolution through tangent-space optimization, matrix-free normal-spectrum estimation for rank expansion, and task-induced geometric initialization. Across language and vision benchmarks, GEAR achieves the best average performance in all evaluated settings with substantially fewer trainable parameters. On LLaMA3-8B, it raises the average commonsense score from 86.61 to 88.45 while reducing trainable parameters from 42.0M to 14.4M.

Title: Constant-Factor Approximations for the Biased Traveling Salesman Problem and Its Path Variant
Author: Jingyang Zhao, Jason William Setiawan, Uman Khalid, Chaoning Zhang, Een-Kee Hong, Hyundong Shin
Text_Content: The metric traveling salesman problem (TSP) is a fundamental problem in combinatorial optimization that asks for a minimum-cost Hamiltonian cycle in a complete undirected graph with $N$ vertices, where edge costs satisfy the triangle inequality. The biased TSP (BTSP) is a natural generalization of the metric TSP, in which the vertex set is partitioned into $k$ subsets: edge costs satisfy the triangle inequality within each subset, while edges crossing the subsets may violate the triangle inequality by a certain bias factor. This model captures scenarios in which distances are metric only locally but may be distorted across different regions or types of vertices. In this paper, we study approximation algorithms for the BTSP and its path variant, the biased traveling salesman path problem (BTSPP), which asks for a minimum-cost Hamiltonian path. Previously, constant-factor approximation algorithms were known only for the case $k=2$. Whether the BTSP and the BTSPP admit constant-factor approximation algorithms for any fixed integer $k>2$ has remained an open question. We resolve this question affirmatively. We show that both the BTSP and the BTSPP admit $O(k)$-approximation algorithms with running time $N^{O(2^k k!)}$. Moreover, for the BTSPP with $k=2$, we propose an improved $(α+2+\varepsilon)$-approximation algorithm, where $α<3/2-10^{-34}$ is the best-known approximation ratio for the metric TSP, improving upon the previous ratio of $4$

Title: AtlasULP: Domain-aware Universal Link Prediction via Relation Atlas
Author: Yujing Liu, Yixin Liu, Yu Zheng, Lianhua Chi, Alan Wee-Chung Liew, Heng Tao Shen, Shirui Pan
Text_Content: Link prediction (LP) is a widely applied task in graph learning. Conventional LP approaches typically follow a dataset-specific paradigm, requiring independent training for each graph and incurring high computational and maintenance costs in large-scale applications. Motivated by these limitations, recent work explores Universal Link Prediction (ULP), aiming to enable training-free inference on arbitrary unseen graphs. However, existing methods primarily rely on subgraph sampling strategies to construct universal representations, which are unable to capture higher-order information due to the exponential growth of higher-order neighborhoods. As a result, they often under-perform on graphs where long-range signals are essential, such as biological networks. Moreover, their prediction models are typically domain-agnostic and lack the ability to adapt to different graph domains, leading to limited generalization. To address these challenges, we propose an Atlas-based Universal Link Prediction framework (AtlasULP), which introduces the relation atlas to capture structural associations between node pairs from both global and local perspectives, enabling a comprehensive characterization of connectivity signals across diverse graph domains. Building upon this representation, we develop a domain-guided prompting ULP model, which generates domain-aware prompt tokens from contextual structures and performs prompt-guided in-context prediction for adaptive link inference. Extensive experiments demonstrate that AtlasULP consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods across diverse graph domains.

Title: GreedTok Is a 0.3287-Approximation for Tokenization, Within 3% of the Best Possible Constant
Author: Kundan Baliga, Aiden Xie, Aditya Byju
Text_Content: A tokenizer's vocabulary is chosen once and used on every input, so it matters how much compression a greedy vocabulary can lose. GreedTok (Lim et al., 2025) picks $k$ tokens one at a time, each time the string that saves the most tokens; its worst-case ratio was open. We prove that GreedTok saves at least 0.3287 of the optimal number of tokens saved, on every corpus and budget, while junction corpora show that no constant above 0.3387 is possible. The lower-bound proof is written out in full and uses no computer certificates. Its key idea is to track the order of greedy's choices: given that order, the pattern greedy leaves inside an optimal token depends on two numbers, and an induction peels off one chosen string at a time; without the order, a needed inequality fails for a 20-character token. Over 256 symbols, GreedTok's ratio exceeds 0.33861 for every $k\ge 104{,}910$, and over $k^c$ symbols with $c<1/2$ it is at least 0.4386 in the limit. We also show that the objective is APX-hard: it has no PTAS unless P = NP.

Title: Slide to Report: Continuous Reporting Symptom-Specific Cybersickness in VR
Author: Purnata Saha, Rifatul Islam, Qiliang He, John Quarles
Text_Content: Cybersickness is often assessed during VR exposure through discrete overall sickness, which cannot capture specific symptoms or their changes over time. Post-exposure questionnaires such as the Simulator Sickness Questionnaire provide symptom-specific measures but cannot be collected during immersion. We investigate whether separating cybersickness into three symptom-specific dimensions -- nausea, oculomotor discomfort, and disorientation -- during immersion provides more informative continuous measurements. We conducted a between-subjects study with 52 participants in a VR-rollercoaster, comparing a three-slider interface with a single-slider interface. Concurrently, participants also completed an auditory Simon task to measure attention. We additionally collected multimodal set of physiological signals, including GSR, ECG, PPG, eye and head tracking. Results show that each slider correlated most strongly with its corresponding SSQ subscale, whereas the single slider correlated with all SSQ subscales. Using three sliders did not significantly affect usability, workload, or attention. We publicly release the multimodal dataset to support future cybersickness research.

Title: Current frontiers in mobility and well-being
Author: Wen-Jing Li, Luo-Luo Jiang, Attila Szolnoki
Text_Content: Human mobility has a profound impact on social structure and collective behavior, which allows individuals to reshape group structures in response to strategy information, acting as a double-edged sword for cooperative behavior. It can both disrupt existing cooperative communities and enable individuals to escape adverse environments and seek high-quality interaction partners. This paper surveys current research progress on the impact of mobility on cooperation within the framework of evolutionary game theory, focusing on specific mechanisms of passive escape, dynamic self-organization driven by active choice, and the core trade-off between migration costs and speed. Mobility, an individual's spatial response to local strategic information that turns location into strategic advantage, influences cooperative evolution by altering interactive information and environmental feedback, consequently affecting sustainable social well-being, such as collective benefits. Under specific conditions, this self-interested behavior at the individual level can foster macrosocial harmony, embodying the unity of individual rationality and collective cooperation. Furthermore, we also discusses inter-layer migration and information routing mechanisms in multilayer networks and extends the perspective to human-machine hybrid systems where mobile agents with information regulation capabilities can serve as information supernodes. Our paper aims to provide a unified framework for understanding mobility as a combined physical and informational driving force in the evolution of cooperation.

Title: Selective Retrieval Routing for Multi-Violation Knowledge Graph Repair
Author: Tung-Wei Lin, Gabe Fierro, Han Li, Tianzhen Hong, Pierluigi Nuzzo, Alberto Sangiovanni-Vincentelli
Text_Content: Knowledge graphs often contain missing or inconsistent facts that undermine the applications built on them. Schema validation detects such violations but does not identify which of several valid repairs recovers the intended graph. External corpora can supply the evidence needed to identify the intended repair, but retrieving from them is costly and not always successful. We propose a framework for selective retrieval in iterative graph repair. An LLM repair agent explores and edits the graph, while a router controls its access to a researcher agent that retrieves external evidence. We extend a violation-injection framework to generate cases with multiple compatible violations and known reference repairs. The agent's repair outcomes on these cases provide supervision for training the deployment-specific router. On two building-automation datasets, researcher access improves repairs for some violations and degrades them for others, with effects differing across deployments. The router uses fewer repair-time tokens than always enabling access in all six evaluation suites. It achieves higher repair $F_1$ than always disabling access in five of six suites.

Title: DiagDBench: Evaluating Agentic LLMs on Interactive Database Diagnosis and Anomaly Remediation
Author: Xinxin Zhao, Rong Kang, Tieying Zhang, Cuiping Li, Hong Chen, Jing Zhang
Text_Content: Database diagnosis and anomaly remediation are essential to reliable database management system (DBMS) operation. Despite advances in large language model (LLM)-based database agents, constructing live DBMS environments that reproduce diverse anomalies at scale remains challenging, limiting the availability of executable samples for database agent training and evaluation. To this end, we introduce DiagDBench, a large-scale benchmark for training and evaluating database agents on interactive diagnosis, anomaly remediation, and optional workload performance optimization across diverse, realistic anomaly scenarios. Each sample pairs a user request, comprising an issue description and an anomaly-verified workload under which the issue was observed, with a self-contained, executable DBMS environment that supports real-time monitoring, interactive diagnosis, remediation, and workload execution. To construct these samples at scale, we propose an LLM-based framework with two complementary pipelines: Manual-Guided Anomaly Synthesis, which sequentially synthesizes user requests, database modifications, and anomaly-injection scripts grounded in DBA manuals and official DBMS documentation; and Incident-Guided Anomaly Reproduction, which reconstructs anomaly samples end to end from real-world enterprise online diagnosis incidents. Built using this framework with sample filtering, expert review, and refinement, DiagDBench comprises 6,940 synthesized training samples and a held-out test set of 454 expert-annotated samples, spanning three hardware configurations, two DBMSs, and three database schemas. Extensive evaluations of database agents powered by multiple LLMs demonstrate that even the best-performing agent, ReAct with GPT-6 Astra, scores only 56.24, whereas most agents score below 45, underscoring the difficulty of DiagDBench.

Title: Frustration-freeness is decidable but unprovable
Author: Naoto Shiraishi
Text_Content: The frustration-free property is valuable in quantum many-body systems, which states that its ground states simultaneously minimize all local interaction terms, even when these terms act on overlapping degrees of freedom. Prominent examples include the AKLT model and Kitaev's toric code model, which serve as paradigmatic models of symmetry-protected topological phases and topological order, respectively. A fundamental question is whether a given Hamiltonian is frustration-free for all system sizes. Here we establish two seemingly contradictory results concerning this decision problem. First, we prove that frustration-freeness is decidable for any fixed local Hilbert space dimension. Specifically, there exists a finite, Hamiltonian-independent system-size cutoff such that frustration-freeness at this cutoff size guarantees frustration-freeness at all system sizes. Second, on the other hand, we also show that there exists a frustration-free Hamiltonian whose frustration-freeness cannot be proved within the standard axioms of mathematics (ZFC). We reconcile these seemingly contradictory results by showing that the cutoff, although finite for each local Hilbert space dimension, is uncomputable as a function of that dimension. Our findings reveal an unexpected fundamental distinction between decidability and provability arising in quantum many-body physics.

Title: Energy-Time Optimal Decoding Using Expander-Graph LDPC Codes and Mesh Network Architecture
Author: Christopher Blake
Text_Content: Within the Thompson VLSI model, the first energy optimal decoding schemes (up to polylogarithmic factors) that also reach clock cycle lower bounds are constructed. Let $N$ be block length. Then, there is an exponential error scaling function and a binary symmetric channel, such that for all $f(N)$ that scales to zero more slowly than this, there is a decoding scheme for this channel with error probability that scales as $O(f(N))$ that has number of clock cycles $T\le O(\sqrt{-\log(f(N)})\text{polylog}(N))$ and energy $E\le O(N\sqrt{-\log(f(N))}\text{polylog}(N))$. This matches fundamental lower bounds up to polylogarithmic factors. The technique uses expander-graph based LDPC codes, a mesh network architecture, and a parallelization technique. The key technical result needed for this is a lemma in graph theory. This lemma is used to show that communication graphs of bounded node degree can be routed through two- and three-dimensional mesh networks without overflowing the memory of any mesh node. Upper bounds are also extended to three dimensions.

Title: When Do Sports Leagues Stop Being Competitive? Bayesian Detection of Competitive-Balance Eras from Match-Level Data
Author: Xinran Li, Maoran Xu, Guanyu Hu
Text_Content: Competitive balance shapes outcome uncertainty, fan interest, and league regulation, yet standard measures summarize realized standings and cannot separate structural ability differences from match-level randomness. We develop a Bayesian framework that infers structural competitive balance from longitudinal match outcomes. Team abilities are obtained by projecting Gaussian auxiliary variables onto a graph-fused l1 polytope whose radius measures total pairwise ability variation. The projection places positive probability on exact ties, so statistically indistinguishable teams form explicit rank tiers. The radius equals realized ability variation whenever the constraint binds, linking it to parity, detectability, and structural inequality. An adaptive finite-regime model lets competitive eras recur, emerge, and disappear while team hierarchies remain season specific. Simulations show accurate recovery of regimes, radii, abilities, and tiers. Applied to 25 English Premier League seasons, the model identifies a persistent shift to a more stratified league beginning in 2005/06, with 2010/11 the only later return to the compressed regime. It also shows that a close title race can coexist with wide league-wide separation and that head-to-head results can separate clubs level on points. The framework gives leagues a model-based measure of balance to inform debates on revenue sharing and financial regulation.

Title: Last-Iterate Convergence of Stochastic Gradient Methods for Unbounded Problems
Author: Kevin Kurian Thomas Vaidyan, Ahmet Alacaoglu, Michael P. Friedlander
Text_Content: Last-iterate convergence guarantees for stochastic gradient methods have attracted significant attention as practical implementations typically return the last iterate instead of an average of the iterates. In this paper, we study two approaches for analyzing the last-iterate convergence of proximal and projected stochastic gradient methods without bounded domain or bounded variance assumptions, where black-box variational inference serves as a running example. Under two related assumptions relaxing the bounded variance, we show near-optimal anytime rate $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(1/\sqrt{T})$ for the last iterate. Moreover, when the horizon $T$ is known, we remove the logarithmic factor and obtain the optimal order $\mathcal{O}(1/\sqrt{T})$, matching the order known under bounded variance or bounded domain assumptions.

Title: Where Do Reported Long-Video QA Gains Come From? A Controlled Audit of Frame Selection, Evidence Injection, and Expert Routing
Author: Shih-Yao Lin
Text_Content: Long-video question answering is usually studied as frame selection: which few frames should a vision-language model see? We introduce VideoRouteAudit, a controlled audit that separates this choice from two alternatives, injecting non-visual evidence and routing to another answering model. It holds the backbone, frame budget, decoding, prompt and grader fixed while varying one decision at a time. On the full Video-MME long bucket (n=900, K=8), no tested selector significantly improves over uniform sampling. The largest selection-only estimate is +1.9 pt (95% CI [-1.2,+5.0]) and our cascade is +1.2 pt [-1.7,+4.1]; all are equivalent to uniform within +/-5 pt. The same contrasts are unstable at the n=200 subset scale commonly used: three of four are up to 3.8x larger, one reverses sign, and resampled 200-item subsets reverse the full-bucket effect's sign in 35.8% of draws. The audit also corrects our own first results. The anomaly-domain "+ASR" arms injected no text, so the pooled +4.7 pt gain was selection plus a development prefix. With transcripts, ASR lowers XD-Violence accuracy by 10.0 pt when appended after the question and not at all when placed before it, and lowers UCF-Crime by 13.0 pt either way; on Video-MME, placing it first adds about 4 pt (7 on Qwen2-VL) to uniform sampling and to the cascade alike (post hoc, unadjusted). Swapping the answering model gives the largest contrast (+15.1 pt on MUSIC-AVQA, +33.3 pt on its worst type), but the same audio-visual expert with its soundtrack silenced keeps 92% of the gain (69% with a mismatched soundtrack), so the contrast is mostly a model swap. Code, per-item predictions and scripts that recompute every statistic are available at https://github.com/mikeslin-ir/long-video-qa-audit.

Title: ELPAC: Endpoint-Anchored Latent Progression with Stage-Varying Multimodal Coordination
Author: Shengxian Ding, Yifei Zhang, Xinyuan Tian, Yuanshuang Guo, Yize Zhao
Text_Content: Aging cohorts increasingly combine imaging, plasma, and cognitive measurements, but most subjects provide only a partially observed cross-sectional snapshot, leaving latent stage, progression subtype, and stage-varying multimodal coordination to be inferred jointly. Existing methods estimate the cohort-level aging process, model covariance under observed covariates, or fuse modalities for prediction. However, they rarely target the joint problem of endpoint-anchored staging and progression-resolved residual coordination across modalities, even though subject staging, subtype assignment, and multimodal interplay are mutually dependent. We introduce ELPAC, a Bayesian framework with two interlocking constructions. The first integrates subtype trajectories backward from clinically reliable endpoint groups along biologically structured velocity components encoding modality-specific monotone direction and optional sequential ordering priors. The second factorizes residual multimodal variation around the inferred stage axis into sparse coordination axes whose loadings and activations expose which multimodal patterns are operative in each subtype and when they emerge, with stage-resolved variation supplying the auxiliary structure for conditional identifiability. We use a scalable amortized variational inference scheme that enables joint posterior inference at cohort scale with single-pass deployment on new subjects. On synthetic data and a harmonized ADNI+NACC/SCAN Alzheimer's cohort, ELPAC demonstrates accurate latent-structure recovery, well-calibrated prediction intervals, and biologically interpretable multimodal coordination programs that differ by subtype.

Title: DC-SQEM: Medial Mesh Extraction by Dual Contouring with Spherical Quadric Error Metric
Author: Bingchuan Li, Ruilong Liu, Tianhao Hu, Congyi Zhang, Ningna Wang, Junfeng Yao, Xiaohu Guo
Text_Content: The medial axis, as a compact representation, describes not only the boundary but also the interior of the shape, and has been widely used in analyzing and simplifying shapes. However, approximating feature-preserving medial axis from unstructured data, such as oriented point clouds, remains challenging due to the lack of explicit connectivity and the presence of noise in the source. We propose DC-SQEM, a dual-contouring-based framework that computes medial meshes (an explicit representation of the medial axis) directly from oriented point clouds without relying on watertight manifold surfaces or volumetric structures. With the help of an adaptive octree, our method fits local medial spheres for each cell based on the Spherical Quadric Error Metric (SQEM). We address several long-standing robustness issues in dual-contouring and mesh extraction, including out-of-cell solutions, unstable feature classification, and redundant topological connections. To this end, we introduce virtual nodes, a feature-downgrading strategy, and a geometry-driven topology-aware cleanup procedure, enabling robust SQEM-based medial dual contouring with clean mesh outputs. Unlike prior point-cloud-based methods that produce either only 1D skeletal structures or incomplete medial features, our method preserves sharp geometric features from the input and reconstructs a complete medial structure, including sheets, curves, seams, and junctions. Compared to restricted-power-diagram-based approaches, our algorithm can handle point clouds as input, without having a strong requirement on water-tightness or manifoldness.

Title: Permanent and Transient Representations for Continual Reinforcement Learning
Author: Nishanth Anand, Doina Precup
Text_Content: Continual Reinforcement Learning (CRL) agents struggle to adapt to new situations while retaining prior knowledge, leading to a stability-plasticity trade-off. One approach to solving this problem is by using complementary learning systems: one for slow, long-term learning and another for quick, transient adaptation. Anand & Precup (2023) instantiated this idea using permanent and transient value functions, but used the same features in both systems. Intuitively, long-term learning should rely more on parametric representations for broad generalization, while transient learning would be best served by non-parametric representations for situation-specific adaptation. In this paper, we explore this idea both theoretically and empirically. By introducing a novel non-parametric approximation for estimating the transient value function in complex tasks, we demonstrate that our method enables online learning and outperforms competitive baselines on image-based tasks and Craftax-Classic, underscoring the effectiveness of our system-level decomposition.

Title: Functional Converses for Private Matrix-Product Retrieval under Library-Wide Decoder-Side Correlation
Author: Malihe Aliasgari, Yousef Nejatbakhsh
Text_Content: We consider private retrieval of the matrix product $A^\top B^{(θ)}$ from replicated $P_c$-colluding servers when $B^{(\ell)}=A+N^{(\ell)}$, with the innovations mutually independent and independent of the user-held $A\in\mathbb{F}_q^{m\times m}$. The servers store the full library, correlated with $A$, which changes both the communication problem and the security definition: a secrecy condition including the stored library cannot hold, as the library itself partly reveals $A$. We therefore measure only additional leakage and require index privacy conditioned on $A$; both reduce to classical notions under independence. For $A$ of rank $k<m$ we prove, with no structural hypothesis on the map, $D^*\geq H(A^\top B^{(θ)}\mid A)/C_{\mathrm{PIR}}(N,P_c,L)-o(km)$, where $C_{\mathrm{PIR}}(N,P_c,L)$ is the replicated $P_c$-colluding private-information-retrieval capacity. The proof rests on a colluding converse for servers storing arbitrary refinements of the demanded messages, whose answers need not be measurable functions of the functional-message library, and a privacy-transfer characterization. Publishing a canonical row-space representative makes the bound achievable for arbitrary independent and identically distributed innovations under a public-setup measure. Under a strengthened observational model (exact correctness, common conditional library support, and full-transcript security), concealment forces $D\geq H(G_m N^{(θ)})/C_{\mathrm{PIR}}$, where $G_m$ spans the linear join of all row spaces in the support of the operand distribution; this extends to vanishing error under a simultaneous-decodability assumption. In the full-rank case product recovery reduces to innovation recovery: $D^*=H(N^{(θ)})/C_{\mathrm{PIR}}+o(m^2)$.

Title: Rule-Guided and Trajectory-Aware Repair for LLM-Based HLS Generation
Author: Xianjing Zhu, Wenqi Lou, Yuanbo Wen, Teng Wang, Lei Gong, Chao Wang, Xuehai Zhou
Text_Content: Large language models (LLMs) offer a promising path for directly generating functionally correct and synthesizable HLS-C from natural-language specifications. However, existing approaches often struggle to turn multi-round tool feedback and reusable HLS knowledge into effective revisions, limiting end-to-end generation success. We propose MementoHLS, an agentic HLS generation framework built around executable and falsifiable dual-memory-guided repair. MementoHLS combines an Executable Repair Contract Library (ERCL), which converts cross-task HLS knowledge into evidence-gated repair actions, with a Reviewer-Grounded Falsification Ledger (RFL), which converts task-local repair history into trajectory evidence to suppress ineffective routes and preserve validated progress. To ensure reliable outcome attribution, a Same-Candidate Reviewer binds Parse, Compile, Testbench (TB), and Synthesis (Synth) outcomes to the corresponding candidate, while a Single-Commit Arbiter commits at most one candidate per round. Evaluated on 94 HLS-Eval and 170 Bench4HLS tasks, MementoHLS improves same-candidate TB$\wedge$Synth pass@1/pass@5 from 41.7%/57.4% to 58.9%/68.1% on HLS-Eval, and from 15.5%/32.9% to 32.4%/50.6% on Bench4HLS, demonstrating substantial improvements in end-to-end HLS generation reliability.

Title: Rethinking Data Selection: The Importance of Coverage over Difficulty in LLM Fine-Tuning
Author: Lalchand Pandia, Kanishka Misra, Allyson Ettinger
Text_Content: Selecting high-quality training data can reduce computation cost for LLM fine-tuning. Prior work on data selection developed a variety of difficulty-based scores, motivated by the intuition that harder examples are more informative. While effective for smaller classification models, we find that such methods often fail to outperform random selection for LLM fine-tuning. Our analysis reveals that random selection performs better because it is more representative of the underlying input space---i.e., has better coverage. To validate the importance of coverage, we implement a simple clustering-based selection method which selects data that is more representative of the underlying input distribution. On a set of diverse single-domain tasks, this method yields performance at or above that of random selection. On the diverse, multi-domain Tülu 3 mixture, where random sampling no longer guarantees a balanced subset, our method outperforms all methods. Overall, our results indicate that prioritizing coverage over difficulty leads to more effective data selection for LLM fine-tuning.

Title: WeightLoop: Weight-Space Programming with Experimental Feedback
Author: Mengran Li, Bo Li, Weijing Zhao, Chengyang Zhang, Boyu Zhang, Jinfeng Xu, Zelin Zang, Victor C. M. Leung, Stan Z. Li
Text_Content: Weight-space programming (WSP) shows that language models can reason about and rewrite neural network weights; recursive self-improvement (RSI) motivates feedback-driven improvement. Models guiding experiments receive concrete feedback: completed assays reveal prediction errors and inform what to test next. We introduce WeightLoop, a framework that turns experimental feedback into persistent updates to deployed predictors. GPT-6 Astra inspects a task specification and the model implementation, then writes a bounded, reusable parameter-editing program. As new measurements arrive, the program identifies prediction discrepancies, validates candidate edits using observed outcomes, and writes the selected changes back to the original model. The editor remains fixed while the predictor evolves, enabling repeated updates without further LLM calls or gradient retraining while preserving the original inference interface. In offline replay, targeted edits improve mean ranking utility in seven of eight endpoint-budget settings (all eight versus random edits) and mean final discovery across three sequential tasks. WeightLoop connects WSP with an RSI-inspired improvement loop, making experimental evidence a direct driver of model change and subsequent decisions.

Title: Asymptotic advantage of quantum one-way and SMP communication for total functions
Author: Dmytro Gavinsky
Text_Content: We exhibit a total Boolean function on n input bits whose bounded-error quantum simultaneous-message (and hence one-way) communication complexity is in O(\sqrt n), whereas its randomised one-way (and hence simultaneous-message) communication complexity is in Ω(n). The same function admits a classical simultaneous-message protocol of cost O(\sqrt n) when the players share O(\sqrt n) EPR pairs.

Title: A nonlinear interface for phase transduction
Author: Linshan Sun, Hao Zhang, Cameron Leary, Alex Amador, Sergio Carbajo
Text_Content: Broadband nonlinear frequency conversion mixes multiple input frequencies, complicating the transfer of programmed spectral phase between widely separated spectral bands. Here we identify and experimentally realize a quasi-linear phase-transduction regime enabled by broad phase-matching acceptance and effective localization of the complex frequency-mixing response. This selectivity can arise from coherent interference without narrowing the pump spectrum. We implement this regime through dispersive four-wave mixing in an argon-filled hollow-capillary fiber, transferring spectral phase from 1032-nm near-infrared signals to 344-nm ultraviolet idlers. Transient-grating frequency-resolved optical gating reveals frequency-inverted, phase-conjugating transfer of quadratic dispersion, localized phase steps, and low-frequency sinusoidal modulation. After correction for the modeled pump-induced phase background, the quadratic and step responses exhibit approximately linear point-by-point correlations. With increasing pump chirp, the transferred phase steps become more sharply preserved, and the fitted phase-transfer gains approach unity, consistent with enhanced effective localization. These results demonstrate quasi-linear spectral-phase transduction in a co-propagating broadband nonlinear interaction without spatially separating its spectral components.

Title: Experimentally Grounded Machine Learning of PrecursorSurface-Reactant Chemistry in Atomic Layer Deposition
Author: Bonwook Gu, Trinh Ngoc Le, Zunair Masroor, Minhyeok Lee, Han-Bo-Ram Lee
Text_Content: Whether a precursor-substrate-reactant combination yields an atomic layer deposition (ALD) process is still settled by trial-and-error experiments. Here we introduce AJIN (ALD Joint Interpretable Network), a machine-learning framework that learns this decision from experimental outcomes. We compiled 560 experimentally observed ALD and area-selective ALD outcomes spanning 76 precursors, 27 substrates, 20 reactants and 25-620 degrees Celsius. Following the ALD cycle, AJIN predicts adsorption from graph-neural-network embeddings of the precursor and substrate with temperature, and deposition by adding the reactant. The best model (CHGNet-MLP) reaches balanced accuracies of 79.2% for adsorption and 84.8% for deposition and transfers partially to unseen precursors. SHAP and ablation analyses show that substrate chemistry governs adsorption, whereas precursor, substrate and reactant all contribute to deposition. Tested against our laboratory's ALD experiments, AJIN correctly predicted 83% of new-substrate cases and 71% of new precursor-substrate adsorption cases, providing an experimentally grounded tool for prioritizing ALD and area-selective ALD chemistries.

Title: Dark-State Coherent Control of Excitons in TMD Monolayers: A Reduced Intravalley Lindblad Framework for WSe$_2$
Author: Mauricio Martinez, Martin A. Mosquera
Text_Content: Dark-state coherence in driven three-level systems underlies electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) and stimulated Raman adiabatic passage (STIRAP). Their performance depends on the coupling topology: in a ladder ($Ξ$) scheme the coherence can bypass a lossy intermediate state, whereas in a $V$ scheme it is carried by two excited states that both decay. We develop a topology-resolved Lindblad framework for driven three-level excitonic manifolds at fixed center-of-mass momentum, in which a single exciton couples to phonons, the radiation field and a dilute exciton gas. The $Ξ$ and $V$ manifolds are selected from the exciton spectrum by systematically screening optical brightness, intra-excitonic dipole strength and state compactness, making the selection reproducible and transferable to other materials. Within this framework, in the $Ξ$ manifold of hBN-encapsulated WSe$_2$, a weak optical pulse, preceded by a terahertz pulse in the counterintuitive STIRAP order, converts the excitation it creates into an optically dark exciton by dark-state following, while the lossy bright intermediate exciton stays nearly empty. The conversion is limited by emission from that intermediate state rather than by non-adiabatic coupling, and is controlled by a single adiabaticity parameter of the terahertz leg. The exchange mean field of the exciton gas shifts the two-photon resonance by more than the conversion tolerates at moderate densities; the center of the cascade transparency window provides an in situ calibration, and we identify the control strengths at which it is true EIT rather than Autler--Townes splitting. The $V$ manifold loses its coherence on the radiative timescale and serves as the unprotected reference. These results provide a minimal, material-specific baseline for dark-state coherent control of excitons in two-dimensional semiconductors in the radiative limit.

Title: Exact $\ell_p$-CVP via Euclidean SVP in Polynomial Space
Author: Jiseung Kim, Minkyu Kim, Hyung Tae Lee
Text_Content: We give a randomized, rank-preserving reduction from exact $\ell_p$-CVP to exact Euclidean SVP for every integer $p\ge2$. For rational inputs of bit length $\ell$ on full-rank lattices $L\subset\mathbb R^N$, the reduction uses $(Cp)^N\poly(p,\ell)$ oracle calls and additional bit operations, where $C$ is an absolute constant. It uses $\poly(p,\ell)$ working space outside the oracle, and all oracle queries have rank $N$ and $\poly(p,\ell)$ bit complexity. For $p=2$, the reduction transfers polynomial-space exact SVP algorithms to exact CVP with $2^{O(N)}\poly(\ell)$ time overhead. Instantiating it with the SVP algorithms of Kannan and of Feng, Gao and Liu yields randomized polynomial-space CVP algorithms running in time $N^{N/(2e)+o(N)}$ and $N^{N/(4e)+o(N)}$, respectively. For every fixed integer $p\ge3$, the same reduction yields exact $\ell_p$-CVP algorithms for arbitrary rational targets either in randomized time and space $2^{O(N)}$, or in randomized time $N^{N/(4e)+o(N)}$ and polynomial space. These algorithmic bounds are up to polynomial factors in $\ell$. The reduction performs local search sequentially over the cosets of \(2L\), where \(L\) is the input lattice, while tracking the excess of the current objective value over the optimum. Within a coset containing a closest vector, midpoint inequalities bound the unknown correction in terms of this excess, which in turn allows us to construct many short corrections that reduce the excess bound by a factor of four. A counting argument shows that these improving corrections form a sufficiently large fraction of the lattice points in a known search region, and a sparsification-based sampler assigns sufficiently large probability to every nonzero vector in that region, using at most one SVP call per sample. For \(p\ge3\), the same framework is extended using a diagonal weighted norm computed from the current point.

Title: A New Characterization of Streaming Decidability of Boolean CSPs Under Deletions
Author: Aditya Bandekar, Amatya Sharma, Santhoshini Velusamy
Text_Content: We characterize the single-pass streaming space complexity of Boolean CSP satisfiability in the strict-turnstile model for every fixed constraint language $Γ$ of $k$-ary Boolean relations that is not trivially satisfiable. Constraints can be inserted or deleted with nonnegative multiplicities; satisfiability is decided for those remaining at the end. While Sharma and Velusamy [ESA 2026] characterized insertion-only complexity via non-redundancy (up to logarithmic factors), we show that strict-turnstile complexity is governed by the integer capturing degree. For $R\subseteq\{0,1\}^k$, let $d_R$ be the minimum degree of an integer-coefficient polynomial vanishing exactly on $R$ over the Boolean hypercube, and set $d_Γ=\max_{R\inΓ}d_R$. On polynomial-length streams, we obtain an $O_k(n^{d_Γ}\operatorname{polylog} n)$-space randomized algorithm and an $Ω_k(n^{d_Γ}/\log n)$ lower bound for all algorithms. Moreover, our algorithm outputs a sparse instance preserving every satisfying assignment. This yields, to our knowledge, the first insertion-only versus turnstile separation for streaming CSPs. It also differs from the Fourier-degree characterization of exact optimization by Kol, Paramonov, Saxena, and Yu [ITCS 2023]. For $k\ge3$, $k$-XOR with literals has three distinct space complexities: $\widetildeΘ(n)$ for insertion-only satisfiability, $\widetildeΘ(n^{\lceil k/2\rceil})$ for strict-turnstile satisfiability, and $\widetildeΘ(n^k)$ for exact optimization in either model.

Title: Quadratic-Time Barriers from Self-Referential SAT
Author: Guangyan Zhou
Text_Content: Under the self-referential $K$-SAT exhaustive-search hypothesis (SRK-ESH), no uniform deterministic algorithm computes exact longest common subsequence or standard edit distance on binary strings in $O(n^{2-η})$ time for any fixed $η>0$, where $n$ is the longer sequence length. The same exclusion holds for one-dimensional dynamic time warping on $\{0,1,2,4,8\}$ with absolute-difference cost and for five-symbol dynamic time warping with the discrete metric. We derive Orthogonal Vectors hardness in polylogarithmic dimension by splitting the variables of the logarithmic-width source formula into two halves. Existing sequence reductions have polynomial overhead in the dimension. Their output lengths and construction times allow a fixed saving in the target exponent to yield a fixed proportional saving in the source exponent.

Title: Take It From Here: Evaluating Coding Agents On Project Takeover
Author: Dingxian Wang, Zhe Fu, Jiaqi Deng, Chao Yin, Ganesh Prabhu, Karthik Gomadam Rajagopal, Darwin Yi, Huan Huo, Guandong Xu, Xianzhi Wang, Andrew Rabinovich, Zhao Chen
Text_Content: Coding agents increasingly collaborate on long-term projects. When taking over a project, they need to recover currently applicable requirements from the interaction history and update them in response to new requests. However, most coding benchmarks do not include long interaction histories, and some evaluations that consider history still do not cover the full process from requirement reconstruction to project delivery. We therefore provide agents with the interaction history, current request, and pre-request project environment, ask them to make the requested changes, and assess takeover performance through delivery tests. Across six model-harness configurations and 37 targets eligible for executable validation, the mean complete-delivery rate under Full History is only 4.95%. We then use requirement atoms to independently diagnose a larger set of takeover targets, examining relevant information identification, pre-request state reconstruction, and current request processing. We further supply correct pre-request or target states to examine the remaining difficulties in requirement processing and project modification. The diagnostics show that none of the six configurations produces fully correct post-request requirement states, and a case illustrates omission of previously recovered constraints during updating. With correct target states supplied, the mean complete-delivery rate is 8.11%, with build and regression pass rates of 96.40% and 90.99%, but target-test success remains 9.01%. These results show difficulties in both forming target requirement states and implementing supplied targets in existing projects. Based on these findings, we introduce ReqMemBench, which combines requirement diagnostics with delivery validation to support systematic evaluation of project takeover.

Title: A componentwise spherical Dirichlet-to-Neumann closure for finite-volume MHD at finite magnetic Reynolds number
Author: Min Ki Jung, Brian Wynne, Francisco Saenz, Yufan Xu, Egemen Kolemen, Yong-Su Na
Text_Content: At finite magnetic Reynolds number, the field induced by a moving conducting fluid or solid extends into open space, so a finite mesh needs an outer boundary condition that represents the decaying exterior field. Magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) codes widely use pseudo-vacuum or truncation at a finite radius. Neither condition is physically correct for a vacuum exterior, but the exact alternatives are costly or limited to simple geometries. We present a Dirichlet-to-Neumann (DtN) closure on a fixed enclosing sphere and release it as part of the open-source multi-region finite-volume solver FreeMHD. The closure matches each Cartesian component of the vector potential to its decaying exterior solution, which retains all three decaying vector-Laplace families. A meshed vacuum buffer connects non-spherical conductors to the sphere. We verify the closure with manufactured modes, sphere free decay, sphere and oblate dynamos, and a freely braking rotor. Under refinement, oblate dynamo thresholds and sphere growth rates converge toward independent spectral references, and the rotor torque matches an exact transient reference. On the same sphere, pseudo-vacuum and truncation give the larger errors predicted by their exterior models. The DtN closure achieves the accuracy of a distant outer boundary with a compact domain.

Title: ArtiVidRM: Verifiable Artifact-as-Rubric Reward Modeling for Explicit Quality Articulation in Video Generation
Author: Caorui Li, Yangguang Ji, Shuxia Lin, Yu Chen, YiCheng Xiao, Yongliang Wu, Zhenxiang Jiang, Licheng Tang, Deng Li, Zhuxuanzi Wang, Jiahao Sun, Chonghan Liu, Lirian Su, Jay Wu, Xu Yang
Text_Content: Reinforcement learning has become an effective approach for improving video generation, but its success depends heavily on reliable reward models. Existing methods either map videos directly to opaque scalar scores or generate free-form rationales that are not explicitly optimized as the basis of the final judgment. We propose ArtiVidRM, a verifiable, artifact-as-rubrics video reward model that follows an observe-then-score paradigm. It first identifies visible generation artifacts and organizes them into a structured artifact list, then uses these artifacts as explicit rubrics for quality assessment. This intermediate representation grounds each score in concrete video-level evidence, making the reward more interpretable and informative for optimization. We further introduce a multi-reward reinforcement learning strategy to jointly optimize artifact prediction and quality assessment. The reward decomposes into complementary objectives that evaluate artifact prediction quality, including semantic coverage and prediction efficiency, together with a pairwise preference objective that supervises quality ranking through score differences. By jointly optimizing the intermediate artifact representation and the downstream preference prediction, the model learns to produce informative artifact lists while improving the accuracy of video quality assessment. Experiments show that ArtiVidRM achieves state-of-the-art performance on video preference benchmarks, provides effective signals for video diffusion optimization, and enables artifact-guided refinement of closed-source video generators.

Title: Executable Specifications as First-Class Independent Verification and Validation Artifacts for Quantum Information and Machine Learning
Author: Ragib Shahariar Ayon, Shibbir Ahmed
Text_Content: Executable specifications make software assumptions explicit and checkable, yet their role in quantum information and machine learning (QIML) remains underexplored. We argue that executable specifications should be treated as first-class artifacts for independent verification and validation (IV&V) of QIML systems. Static analysis, testing, simulation, and runtime checking can provide evidence about QIML behavior, while Design by Contract shows that selected quantum-state, measurement, and statistical properties can be expressed as checkable conditions. However, adapting existing methods for specification inference and assessment from conventional and machine-learning software to QIML raises several challenges, notably limited evidence for deriving generalizable specifications, cross-stage and probabilistic behavior, repository-scale reasoning across hybrid workflows, and weak behavioral oracles. We characterize these challenges and identify research directions for QIML corpora, specification semantics, repository-level analysis, and specification assessment.

Title: Reducing Representational Interference in Retrieval Embeddings with Trainable Prefix Tokens
Author: Seongtae Hong, Youngjoon Jang, Jungseob Lee, Chanjun Park, Heuiseok Lim
Text_Content: Embedding models compress variable-length text into fixed-size vector representations, but this compression can entangle semantic content with residual token-level information, such as artifacts arising from attention sink behavior. We propose a simple method that prepends trainable [DUMP] tokens to the input during embedding model training. The method keeps the model architecture, pooling strategy, and training loss unchanged, while optimizing the added tokens through the standard contrastive retrieval objective. By introducing trainable prefix positions that interact with regular tokens during encoding, [DUMP] tokens help reduce the influence of residual or uninformative token-level signals on the final retrieval representation. Experiments on standard retrieval and long-context benchmarks show that our method consistently improves over finetuned baselines across encoder and decoder embedding models. Further analysis shows that [DUMP] tokens alter token-level activation and attention patterns associated with low-information tokens. These results suggest that trainable prefix tokens provide a lightweight way to improve retrieval representations.

Title: Code, Commits, and Complexity in the GenAI Era: A Longitudinal Study of Team-Based Capstone Projects
Author: Asma Shakil, Claus Brabrand, Paul Denny
Text_Content: Generative AI tools are now widely available to students, but little is known about how team-based project codebases have changed since they appeared. This matters when project courses use repository activity as evidence of progress and learning. Existing studies have largely examined self-reports, controlled tasks, or short individual assignments, leaving open questions around how student codebases evolve in authentic project settings. We present a ten-semester analysis of N=260 capstone team repositories from 2021 to 2025, spanning pre- and post-AI cohorts. We examine three dimensions: code size (lines of code), code characteristics (comment density, error-handling density, and cyclomatic complexity), and development behaviour (commit volume, edit size, and commit frequency). We find that end-of-semester codebases roughly triple, from about 3.4 KLOC in 2021--2023 to about 10 KLOC in 2024--2025. Code characteristics show a clear decoupling: cyclomatic complexity and error-handling density increase, while comment density does not. Later cohorts commit far more often and in greater volume, but individual commit sizes are largely unchanged, suggesting a shift in development rhythm rather than edit granularity. Most changes appear from 2024 onwards and are not uniformly monotonic. We did not directly observe AI use, so we report these as changes that coincide with increased GenAI availability rather than as effects of AI use. Our findings highlight the need to reconsider how student-produced artefacts are used and assessed in project courses.

Title: Robust Ranking of Port Impacts from Impending Tropical Cyclones: A Two-Stage Recommendation System
Author: Chenchen Kuai, Shixuan Tang, Chaolun Ma, Xiaoqiang Kong, Xiubin Bruce Wang, Yunlong Zhang, Zihao Li
Text_Content: When a tropical cyclone (TC) threatens several ports, preparedness planning depends on anticipating which ports are likely to be affected and where disruptions may last longest. Limited historical observations at individual ports and uncertainty in landfall location make these relative impacts difficult to estimate. We use a two-stage recommendation framework that first selects candidate ports based on their proximity to the expected landfall location and then ranks them by their estimated number of impact days. Using AIS-derived impact days for 37 ports and 31 TCs in the Gulf of Mexico study region, we compare three ways of representing port--cyclone interactions: pairwise feature interactions, tree-based feature combinations, and explicit feature crosses combined with learned embeddings. In tests on Hurricanes Nicole and Ian, the retrieval stage consistently identifies all observed affected ports under landfall uncertainty. Among the ranking models, Wide & Deep Learning achieves the closest agreement with the observed port rankings. Its mean ranking agreement exceeds that of the distance-based baseline by 85.5% for Nicole and 55.5% for Ian and is less sensitive to uncertainty in the landfall location. These rankings could help port authorities prioritize post-cyclone inspections and allocate recovery resources across ports threatened by the same event.

Title: Provably Efficient Representation Learning for Low-Rank CMDPs
Author: Kaixuan Liu, Guojun Xiong, Shengpu Tang, Wanyun Si, Jian Li
Text_Content: We study representation learning in low-rank Constrained Markov Decision Processes (CMDPs), where both value and reward functions are approximated by a set of unknown representation vectors, and the transition dynamics admit a low-rank factorization. The objective is to maximize expected cumulative rewards while complying with constraints on the expected cumulative utility. To achieve this, we propose \texttt{MFRLC} (Model-Free Representation Learning for Low-Rank CMDP), a model-free algorithm that uses a primal-dual scheme to effectively balance reward regret and constraint violations. To the best of our knowledge, \texttt{MFRLC} is the first representation-learning method for low-rank CMDPs that combines the Least-Squares Value Iteration with Upper Confidence Bound (LSVI-UCB) and primal-dual techniques. \texttt{MFRLC} further enhances value function estimation with bonuses for function approximation and learns the mapping from representations to value functions directly, avoiding explicit estimation of the transition kernel. We prove that, with high probability, \texttt{MFRLC} achieves $\widetilde O(K^{3/4})$ reward regret and cumulative constraint violation over $K$ deployment rounds, independent of the size of the state space. To our knowledge, these are the first sublinear regret and violation guarantees for CMDPs with unknown features.

Title: Householder Motion Embedding: Noise Modulation for Motion-Controllable Video Generation
Author: Tao Jun Lin, Jinhong Ni, Ruyi Zha, Yifu Wang, Xibin Song, Pan Ji, Hongdong Li
Text_Content: Diffusion models for video generation have achieved remarkable success, yet precise motion control under explicit user guidance remains challenging. Recent noise-warping methods introduce temporal correlations by warping the noise according to the user-provided motion signal. However, standard spatial warping generally disrupts the noise's i.i.d. Gaussian structure, requiring distribution correction, such as Jacobian-based correction, but at a substantial computational overhead. We propose Householder Motion Embedding (HME), which encodes the motion signal into the noise through a sequence of Householder reflections that together form an orthogonal transformation applied to each location's channel vector. HME exactly preserves the spatial Gaussian structure within each frame while introducing cross-frame correlations that promote temporally consistent video. HME is agnostic to the network architecture and integrates directly into standard video diffusion fine-tuning pipelines. Experiments on different scenarios show that HME matches or outperforms the state of the art, while achieving a 2.7x speedup over noise warping. These results demonstrate that channel-space Householder transformations offer a principled and efficient alternative to noise warping for motion-controllable video generation.

Title: An Ordering Optimization for Fruit-Vegetable in High-Density Environment based on Genetic Algorithm
Author: Jaehwi Seol, Jeonghyeon Pak, Hyoung Il Son
Text_Content: This paper presents a robotic harvesting method that combines RGB-D fruit localization, GA-based harvest ordering, and waypoint-based robot motion in dense and unstructured crop environments. The global RGB-D camera provides 3D fruit positions for ordering, while the end-effector-mounted camera provides close-range observation during execution. The GA determines the harvesting sequence, and static or dynamic waypoints define the intermediate robot motion. The method was evaluated in a controlled laboratory testbed and in four-, five-, and six-fruit field conditions. GA solutions were compared with exhaustive enumeration, and both waypoint offsets were examined by parameter sensitivity analysis. Continuous execution reduced unnecessary Home-return motion, while the dynamic waypoint changed with the remaining fruit distribution without changing the GA sequence. In the field evaluation, the dynamic-waypoint continuous strategy produced 40 collision events and a 70.7% target-approach success rate, compared with 55 collision events and 65.3% for the static-waypoint continuous strategy.

Title: How do Transformers Perform Low-Level Control In-Context?
Author: Ebonye Smith, Aidan Andrews, Phoenix Wilson, Alexis Frias, Ayush Pandey, Gireeja Ranade
Text_Content: One of the remarkable abilities of Transformer-based neural networks is in-context learning. This motivates us to think about "in-context" control. Can we control a system knowing only (1) that it belongs to a particular family of systems and (2) some data on system evolution (provided as the context trajectory) but no specific parameter information? Specifically, we investigate the ability of Transformer-models to perform "in-context" control of unstable, nonlinear dynamical systems, where context consists only of the unforced system dynamics. We leverage a multi-head, GPT-2-style architecture, and we evaluate performance for two classical nonlinear systems -- the cartpole system and the two-link acrobot system, where the system parameters are unknown to the Transformer. We consider a setting where trajectories from an expert controller are available at training time but not at inference time. Here, we identify training techniques that are essential to train Transformers to perform low-level control. Through an analysis over checkpoints, we show that in-context control is possible, and the learned policy performance generally improves as context increases. Furthermore, the Transformer models can generalize to stabilize systems that are out-of-distribution.

Title: Patch-Based Generalized Neural Texture Upscaling
Author: Shin Fujieda, Takahiro Harada
Text_Content: We propose a lightweight neural texture upscaling method. A single generalized MLP is trained on a diverse collection of texture patches and integrated into the texture sampling stage, upscaling low-resolution textures on-the-fly at rendering time. Because the model is generalized rather than overfit to specific content, no per-asset training is required - the same model applies to any existing scene without modifying texture data or the asset pipeline. Storing lower-resolution base textures reduces disk footprint, upscaling at sampling time eliminates the need to store high-resolution textures in VRAM, and sharing a single set of model weights across all textures ensures non-divergent GPU execution.
